text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- 1997 national health budget up 1.3 percent over 1996.
-- November agricultural prices down 1.9 percent over October.
-- IBCA ups Corifrance to A- from BBB+.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Anti-smoking league sues Seita over two cancer deaths.
-- Euro parity set at 6.66 francs.
-- GAN borrows and transfers 2.3 billion francs to ailing property subsidiary.
L'AGEFI
-- Most French economists see 1997 GDP growth at around two percent.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- 1997 government bond/T-bill issues should reach a record 689.7 billion francs.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- France bans asbestos on January 1.
-- Bank of France monetary policy council would prefer extending Jean Boissonnat's term and bring in Jean-Rene Bernard to replace outgoing Bruno de Maulde, but others names are floating around.
LE PARISIEN
-- Monetary Policy Council member Paul Marchelli expects 1997 GDP to grow by over 2.5 percent.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Paul Marchelli says government will probably fill two vacancies on Monetary Policy Council next Friday.
